candidates.term: The Rival at the Month Gate
candidates.defline: The Rival stands at your Month Gate, in plain view: at work people see your nerve before anything else.
candidates.reading: The working world sees your competitive side first, the colleague who volunteers whenever there is a contest to enter. Because winning in the open is how you prove your worth, you rise fastest where results are ranked and stall where credit is pooled. You make allies quickly and lose them almost as quickly, and your worst setbacks have come through bets you shared with someone else.
candidates.teaser: At work you compete the way others breathe, and people feel it. Your career rises fastest in open contests, and slowest wherever the prize must be split.

domain_readings.Career: Your career runs on open contest: rankings, commissions, arenas with scoreboards, and you visibly alive in them. Vague collectives dull you and clear stakes sharpen you. Choose fields where winning is measurable and yours. The nerve that unsettles quiet offices is exactly what podiums pay for.
domain_readings.Social: Work fills your social ledger: allies made fast, rivals made faster, both rotated often. The respect you earn in competition outlasts the friendships it costs. Keep one rival close and honored. They are the only colleague who will always tell you the truth.

candidates.life_chapter: Your rising chapter is a tournament: the prime decades hand you contests, and you convert them into rank while steadier people convert hours. Expect wins that arrive in public and losses that arrive through partners. Compete openly, split prizes beforehand, and the era pays your nerve well.
candidates.relations: Rivals and running mates are this seat’s people: the peers you measure against, the partners whose bets you share. Parents watch these decades with held breath. The relationships thrive on declared terms. Ambiguity is the only opponent that reliably beats you.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the contests pass unentered: nerve present, number never taken. Sign up for one scored thing this quarter and let the era see you.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, everything becomes a heat: meetings, friendships, lunch. Save the competing for arenas that pay.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, the colleague becomes the mark: wins counted in someone else’s losses.
candidates.health_line: Adrenaline is your work fuel and your work tax: the body scores every contest. Cool down as deliberately as you compete.

Career.headline: You rise fastest where the score is public.
Career.recognition: You come alive in work that ranks people openly, commissions and targets and anything with a clear winner. Because you need proof that you are winning, a vague team goal leaves you flat and restless. You unsettle quieter colleagues without meaning to, and you do your best work where nobody minds.
Career.lived: Since your late teens your best jobs have been the ones with a clear score, sales figures or rankings or a promotion race. You have left at least one shared project because the prize was never clearly divided, and you have done better alone since.

Social.headline: Your circle is full of rivals you respect.
Social.recognition: Most of your friends come from work, and many of them started as people you competed against. Because you respect anyone who can beat you, your closest bond at work is with a former rival. You lose friends over contests more easily than most people, and you keep the ones who competed fairly.
Social.lived: From your late teens you have made friends through competition, in teams and offices and courses where everyone was ranked. More than once a friendship ended when you won, and you have kept the rival who took a loss well.
